The Swift SDK's SwiftUI kit. One modifier gates an iPhone, iPad or Mac app and runs every screen the
license needs: Welcome, the one sign-in form, the key field with its live verdict, Replace a
device, the blocking states with their fixes, offline grace and the toast. On iOS and iPadOS 26
the controls are Liquid Glass; on 18 the same layout runs on system materials. Every screen is
drawn from **PolarisKeyUICore**, a SwiftUI-free presentation core that runs the shared
[UI state matrix](/docs/reference/corpus/) for every component, so a UIKit app or a UI of your
own gets the same states, copy and actions. The rest of the Swift SDK is on the
[Swift](/docs/build/sdks/swift/) page; the Mac scenes are under [macOS](#macos).

<KitFacts kit="swiftui" />

## Install

The kit is two products of the `polaris-key.PolarisKey` package in Polaris Key's Swift registry
([Installing the SDKs from the feeds](/docs/build/install/)). The package's floors are
iOS 18, macOS 15, tvOS 18 and visionOS 2.

```swift title="Package.swift"
// swift-tools-version: 6.0
import PackageDescription

let package = Package(
    name: "MyApp",
    platforms: [.iOS(.v18), .macOS(.v15)],
    dependencies: [
        .package(id: "polaris-key.PolarisKey", from: "0.9.3")
    ],
    targets: [
        .target(name: "MyApp", dependencies: [
            .product(name: "PolarisKeyUI", package: "polaris-key.PolarisKey"),      // the views
            .product(name: "PolarisKeyUICore", package: "polaris-key.PolarisKey"),  // no SwiftUI
        ])
    ]
)
```

A Mac app that updates through Sparkle adds `PolarisKeyUpdate`, and `PolarisKeyUpdateUI` for the kit's update window ([macOS](#macos)).

The kit bundles Rubik and JetBrains Mono (both OFL) and registers them itself.

## The one-line flow

```swift
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import SwiftUI

struct MyScene: Scene {
    let client: PolarisKeyClient

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup { ContentView().polarisKeyGate(client) }
    }
}

struct ContentView: View {
    var body: some View { Text("Licensed") }
}
```

`.polarisKeyGate` starts its model, shows the product's icon until the first check answers (never
the sign-in screen during a cached-session check), re-renders on `client.events` and refreshes when
the scene becomes active. It takes `KitGateOptions` for what the build offers (key entry, offline
activation, a trial, restore, enrolment) and how sign-in presents (`signInPresentation: .inline`,
the default, `.sheet` or `.browser`; `replace: .inline` or `.browser`). An app that opens sign-in
from its own menu uses the sheet. The app holds a `PolarisKeyGateModel` and gives it to
`PolarisKeyGate(model:)`:

```swift
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import PolarisKeyUICore
import SwiftUI

struct MyApp: View {
    @State private var model: PolarisKeyGateModel
    @State private var signingIn = false

    init(client: PolarisKeyClient) {
        _model = State(initialValue: PolarisKeyGateModel(client: client))
    }

    var body: some View {
        PolarisKeyGate(model: model) {
            Button("Sign in") { signingIn = true }
                .polarisKeySignIn(isPresented: $signingIn, model: model)
        }
    }
}
```

## Piecemeal

Every screen and part is public and takes the core's `KitScreen` for its component, so it can sit
anywhere inside `PolarisKeyScope(model:)`, which puts the resolved theme, copy and product icon in
the environment:

- screens: `BootView`, `WelcomeView`, `ActivateView`, `SignInView` (with its steps
  `SignInMethodsView`, `SignInHandoffView`, `LicenseChoiceView`, `ReplaceDeviceView`),
  `DeviceLimitView`, `StatusScreenView`, `GraceBannerView`, `UpdatePromptView`,
  `UpdateProgressView`, `ReleaseNotesView`, `PaywallView`, `EntitlementGate` and `ToastView`;
- panes for your own settings `Form`: `AccountAndLicenseSection`, `DevicesSection` and
  `SettingsSection`;
- parts: `ProductIcon`, `MonogramIcon`, `ProductHeader`, `KeyField`, `CodeDisplay`,
  `CountdownRing`, `SeatMeter`, `DeviceRow`, `StatusPill`, `LoadingIndicator`, `ProgressBar` and
  `PoweredBy`.

A `PolarisKeyStyle` replaces or wraps one component's body the way a `ButtonStyle` does, with the
component's state, copy lines and actions in its configuration:

```swift
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import SwiftUI

struct MyWelcome: PolarisKeyStyle {
    func makeBody(configuration: PolarisKeyStyleConfiguration) -> some View {
        VStack {
            Text(configuration.text("welcome.title") ?? "")
            configuration.content   // the kit's own Welcome, below your header
        }
    }
}

struct StyledApp: View {
    let client: PolarisKeyClient

    var body: some View {
        Text("Licensed").polarisKeyGate(client).welcomeStyle(MyWelcome())
    }
}
```

## iPad and identity

On an iPad, a tall, wide window centers a focused step (sign-in, Replace a device, a blocking
state) instead of stretching it across the window. Every screen carries the product header (icon or monogram, then the
name) from the presentation, and a product with no name reads "Welcome". Boot draws the loading
shimmer after the 250 ms grace, and it stays still under Reduce Motion.

## macOS

The same gate runs on a Mac (macOS 15 and later), in Mac proportions: the Welcome window splits the product's identity from the form at 760 by 520 pt and up, and the sign-in sheet is one 440 pt form fitted to its content (`.presentationSizing(.fitted)`). Two more pieces are Mac-only: a Settings tab and the app-menu commands. Nothing needs a platform check; the iOS build leaves them out.

```swift
#if os(macOS)
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import SwiftUI

struct MacScenes: Scene {
    let client: PolarisKeyClient

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup { Text("Licensed").polarisKeyGate(client) }
            .commands { PolarisKeyCommands(client) }
        Settings { PolarisKeySettingsPane(client) }
    }
}
#endif
```

`PolarisKeySettingsPane` is one Settings tab, Account: the license, Devices, the version with **Check for Updates…**, the publisher's channel and automatic-update rows, the catalog's managed settings, and **Sign Out…** behind a confirmation. It takes `handlers:` (`KitSettingsHandlers`: `manage`, `autoUpdate`, `selectChannel`, `signedOut`), `options:` (`KitSettingsOptions`), a `cloudSync:` status line for the Cloud Sync row and a `checkForUpdates:` closure. `PolarisKeyCommands` adds **Check for Updates…** and **Manage License…** under About and **Sign Out…** after Settings…; it takes `theme:`, `handlers:` and `checkForUpdates:`. Both also take a `PolarisKeySettingsModel` you hold (`model:`), for previews.

**Replace a device.** Set `KitGateHandlers.replaceDevice` to a closure that receives the chosen device's id, and the sign-in form lists your devices with Replace…. Without it the form offers the browser path.

### Settings with other tabs

Put the pane in your own `TabView`. **Manage License…** sets `PolarisKeySettingsRoute.shared.selection` to `PolarisKeySettingsPane.tag` before it opens Settings, so bind your selection to it. A Settings scene that holds only the pane needs nothing.

```swift
#if os(macOS)
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import SwiftUI

struct Preferences: View {
    let client: PolarisKeyClient
    @State private var route = PolarisKeySettingsRoute.shared

    var body: some View {
        TabView(
            selection: Binding(
                get: { route.selection ?? "general" },
                set: { route.selection = $0 })
        ) {
            Text("General").tabItem { Text("General") }.tag("general")
            PolarisKeySettingsPane(client)
        }
        .frame(width: 650)
    }
}
#endif
```

### Updates on a Mac

**Check for Updates…** goes to `PolarisKeyUpdateHook.present`. With no handler set, the pane and the menu check on the client and say "You're up to date" or what failed. Two ways to set it, and both keep Sparkle's feed, signature check and install.

The kit's driver. Add the `PolarisKeyUpdateUI` product and pass `PolarisSparkleUserDriver` to `PolarisSparkle.start`. The driver draws Sparkle's flow in one utility window (permission, found, download, extracting, ready, up to date, and an error with Try Again), answers Sparkle only from a control the person pressed, and sets the hook itself. `PolarisSparkleUserDriver.Options` takes a theme and a window title; with `presentsWindow: false` you place `UpdateWindowView(model:)` yourself.

```swift
#if os(macOS)
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUpdate
import PolarisKeyUpdateUI

@MainActor
func startUpdates(_ client: PolarisKeyClient) async throws -> PolarisSparkle {
    let driver = PolarisSparkleUserDriver(client: client)
    return try await PolarisSparkle.start(client: client, userDriver: driver)
}
#endif
```

Your own `SPUUserDriver`. Pass it as `userDriver:`, and set the hook to start the check. A driver that adopts `PolarisSparkleUpdaterAware` is handed the updater.

```swift
#if os(macOS)
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import PolarisKeyUpdate
import Sparkle

@MainActor
func startUpdates(_ client: PolarisKeyClient, driver: any SPUUserDriver) async throws
    -> PolarisSparkle
{
    let sparkle = try await PolarisSparkle.start(client: client, userDriver: driver)
    PolarisKeyUpdateHook.present = { sparkle.updater.checkForUpdates() }
    return sparkle
}
#endif
```

`PolarisSparkle.updater` is set on both paths; `controller` is `nil` when you pass a driver. Keep the returned object for the app's lifetime, and keep `SUPublicEDKey` in your `Info.plist` ([Swift SDK](/docs/build/sdks/swift/)).

### Hosting in AppKit

An AppKit app hosts the same views. Put the gate in an `NSHostingController` for the window's content. For the sign-in form as a sheet, host `SignInView` in its own window and call `beginSheet`; the SwiftUI `.polarisKeySignIn` modifier does the sizing for you, and here you size it. The form is 440 pt wide and as tall as its content.

```swift
#if os(macOS)
import AppKit
import PolarisKey
import PolarisKeyUI
import PolarisKeyUICore
import SwiftUI

@MainActor
final class MainWindowController {
    let model: PolarisKeyGateModel
    let window: NSWindow

    init(client: PolarisKeyClient) {
        model = PolarisKeyGateModel(client: client)
        let gate = PolarisKeyGate(model: model) { Text("Licensed") }
        window = NSWindow(contentViewController: NSHostingController(rootView: gate))
    }

    /// The sign-in form as a sheet over the main window, from your own menu item.
    func presentSignIn() {
        var sheet: NSWindow?
        let model = self.model
        let window = self.window
        let form = PolarisKeyScope(model: model) {
            SignInView(model: model) {
                if let sheet { window.endSheet(sheet) }
            }
        }
        .frame(width: 440)
        .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
        let host = NSHostingController(rootView: form)
        host.sizingOptions = [.preferredContentSize]
        let panel = NSWindow(contentViewController: host)
        sheet = panel
        model.route = .signIn
        window.beginSheet(panel) { [model] _ in model.cancelSignIn() }
    }
}
#endif
```

The gate model drives both windows, so a sign-in finished in the sheet clears the gate behind it. `cancelSignIn()` runs when the sheet ends however it ends. To show the Settings tab from AppKit, host `PolarisKeySettingsPane(client)` in a `TabView` in your preferences window controller.

## Headless

`PolarisKeyUICore` imports no SwiftUI. `PolarisKeyGateModel` is an `@Observable` view of the client
as `KitInputs`, with the actions every screen needs (`submitKey()`, `beginSignIn()`,
`reopenBrowser()`, `useCode()`, `cancelSignIn()`, `useDifferentKey()`, `signOut()`, `refresh()`).
`KitStates` holds one pure function per component from `KitInputs` to a `KitScreen` (its state, its
copy lines with their arguments, and its actions); `KitCopy` formats a line in any launch locale.
A UI of your own binds to the model, or fills `KitInputs` from its own state and calls `KitStates`.

```swift
import PolarisKeyUICore

@MainActor
func keyFieldLine(model: PolarisKeyGateModel) -> String? {
    let screen = KitStates.activate(model.inputs)
    switch screen.state {
    case .parsed:
        return KitCopy.bundled.format(screen.line("part.keyField.forProduct")!, locale: "en")
    case .deviceLimit:
        return nil  // the neutral callout, and Replace a device
    default:
        return nil
    }
}
```

`PolarisKeyPreviewState.all` names a fixture input for every state, for `#Preview`s and your own
tests: `PolarisKeyPreview(.named(.welcome, "default")!)` draws one; `PolarisKeyGallery()` lists
them all.

The product's identity comes from your theme, then the product's registered presentation through
the SDK's presentation source, then the app bundle; with no icon the kit draws a monogram, never a
Polaris Key mark.

## Theming

`.polarisKeyTheme(PolarisKeyTheme(…))` sets every field of the [theme](/docs/build/ui/theming/):
`preset` (`.polarisKey`, or `.native` for the system fonts, the app's tint and the system grounds),
`colorScheme`, `accent` (`.product`, `.core` or `.color("#…")`, always through the contrast
resolver), `radius`, `typography` (Rubik by default, `.system`, or a family you register),
`density`, `motion`, `ambient`, `product`, `copy`, `locale` and `poweredBy`. `poweredBy` draws the
Locker line as the account pane's last section footer; the badge is `PolarisPoweredByAttribution(style: .badge)` on your about or credits screen. Never on the gate.

## Localization

The kit reads the generated catalog in nine locales from `PolarisKeyUICore`'s `kit-copy.json`,
formatted by the core (plurals, the form factor's word: "this iPhone", "this iPad"). `copy` in the
theme overrides a key per locale, falling back key by key: the locale's override, the locale's
table, the English override, then English.

## States to handle

Whatever the screens, the app has to handle these gate states, on a Mac as on an iPhone. If you draw your own UI, read each line from the copy catalog.

    { state: "Activate", copyKey: "gate.needs-activation" },
    { state: "Update required", copyKey: "gate.version-too-old" },
    { state: "Build not on this license", copyKey: "gate.version-too-new" },

  ]}
/>

## Sample

`examples/ui/swiftui/` is Tidewater Studio as an XcodeGen app: with no arguments it lists every
preview state; `-pkeyState Welcome.default` draws one; `--live` gates a list of sessions with
`.polarisKeyGate` against a real Worker (`PKEY_PRODUCT`, `PKEY_BASE_URL` and the pins in
`PKEY_PINS`). Its `run.sh` renders every state on the iOS simulator, runs
`performAccessibilityAudit` on each render and compares it with the committed baselines.
